scenes.headline: How a three-tier agent splits its work
scenes.sub: Code, a decision model, a reasoning model, and why the middle isn't between.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Orchid! Agents now split three ways: code, a decision model, and a reasoning model. Here's how the split works.

scenes.text: The tiers differ by output type, not difficulty. And the decision tier can't see across its options, so code builds every relation for it.
scenes.mark: code builds every relation for it
scenes.say: The tiers differ by output type, not difficulty. And the decision tier can't see across its options, so code builds every relation for it.

scenes.title: The sorting rule is a type test

items.say: An exact rule, like stopping after ten actions, belongs in code.

items.text: Picks, scores, yes or no: Jev
items.say: If it picks, scores, or answers yes or no, it goes to the decision model, Jev.
If it creates text, it stays with the reasoning model.

steps.say: Stanley, a coding agent built this way, shows it. Code computes facts first, and gates which workflows may be offered.
Jev gets one question: pick a workflow, or cannot tell. It returns a probability for each option.
Then fixed thresholds decide, including a margin: the top pick must beat the runner-up by point one five.
Fail a test and the outcome is cannot tell. The model's answer is only an input to a decision that code makes.

scenes.title: A robot arm, one axis at a time

steps.label: One joint move: 81 combinations
steps.say: A robot arm's move is a joint choice across X, Y, Z and the gripper: eighty-one combinations. The xArm7 harness never asks for one.

steps.label: Four questions, one sign each
steps.note: code picks a 2, 4 or 18 mm step
steps.say: Instead it asks four separate questions, one sign per axis. The model chooses direction; code chooses distance, and checks the workspace.

scenes.label: faster per call, measured in the xArm7 trial, against 193.6x claimed
scenes.note: one seed, one trial; the cost ratio broadly survives
scenes.say: The headline says up to a hundred and ninety-three point six times faster. Measured per call in that trial: four point five seven.

scenes.text: Making a decision cheap pushes the hard work back into deterministic code, where you can read it.

recap: Sort by output type: rule, choice, or text
Code builds relations; the model answers alone
Thresholds, not the model, make the decision
scenes.say: To recap: sort by output type, let code build relations, and let thresholds decide.
